source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Missed clonidine doses usually cause sustained hypotension and bradycardia, so the elevated home pressure is probably unrelated to medication interruption.","B":"Abrupt clonidine withdrawal typically lowers sympathetic activity, making severe hypertension unlikely even when headache and tachycardia are present.","C":"Clonidine can be stopped without tapering once several doses are missed, because clinically important withdrawal effects are not expected in treated hypertension.","D":"Abrupt clonidine withdrawal can cause rebound hypertension with headache and tachycardia, so clonidine should be tapered gradually instead of stopped suddenly."}}
source_row.rationale: Current clonidine labeling warns that abrupt discontinuation can cause rebound hypertension and withdrawal symptoms that include headache and tachycardia; gradual tapering is recommended. Option D matches the presentation. Option A describes the opposite hemodynamic pattern. Option B incorrectly says sympathetic activity falls. Option C incorrectly states that clinically important withdrawal is not expected and that tapering is unnecessary.
